effect_size: SOC +15-25% in 2-3 yrs; pollinator visits +30-50%; microbial biomass +20-40%
intervention: Legume-based cover crops + intercropping (e.g., chickpea/lentil with wheat, no bare fallow)
mechanism: Biological N-fixation lowers C:N, adds labile root exudates feeding microbes; continuous floral resources bridge pollinator gaps in monoculture; living roots cut erosion and moisture loss.
source: FAO Soils & Agroecology (2017, 2022); Poeplau & Don meta-analysis, Global Change Biology (2015)
title: Legume cover/intercrop restores SOC and pollinators in cereal monocultures

effect_size: SOC +0.2-0.5 tC/ha/yr; soil water +15-30%; bird/insect richness +40-60% vs monoculture
intervention: Parkland agroforestry: scattered native N-fixers (Prosopis cineraria / Faidherbia albida) at 10-20 trees/ha + crop alleys
mechanism: Deep roots hydraulic-lift water; leaf litter builds SOC; canopy creates microclimate (-2-4C heat stress) and stepping-stone habitat breaking fragmentation.
source: FAO Agroforestry (2019); IPCC AR6 WGIII Ch.7 AFOLU; Bargues-Tobella et al., 2020
title: Semi-arid parkland agroforestry for carbon, water, habitat

effect_size: SOC +10-20% in 3-5 yrs; earthworms x1.5-2; runoff -40%
intervention: No-till + residue retention (30%+ cover, Happy Seeder style)
mechanism: Undisturbed fungal hyphae + aggregate protection stabilizes carbon; residue mulch buffers pH and moisture, shelter for ground beetles/spiders.
source: IPCC AR6 WGIII; FAO Conservation Agriculture; Pittelkow et al. meta-analysis
title: Conservation tillage protects soil biota

effect_size: Soil moisture +25-40%; crop survival in drought +30%; amphibian/insect refugia +50%
intervention: Rainwater harvesting: contour bunds + farm ponds + mulch pits (5-10% area)
mechanism: Concentrates scarce rainfall into infiltration zones; rewets soil profile extending growing season; ponds double as dry-season wildlife water.
source: UNCCD Drought Toolbox; FAO Water Harvesting; IPCC AR6 Adaptation
title: In-situ water harvesting buffers low rainfall

effect_size: Pollination +20-40%; pest control -30% pesticide; bird richness +25%
intervention: 5-10% beetle banks + native hedgerows + wildflower strips on field margins
mechanism: Linear woody/floral corridors reconnect fragments (island biogeography); overwintering habitat for predators/parasitoids; unfamiliar to pests but familiar to pollinators.
source: IPBES 2019; Dainese et al., Science Advances (2019); UK CEH long-term trials
title: Field-margin corridors defeat fragmentation cheaply

effect_size: pH toward 6.0-7.5 in 1-2 seasons; microbial diversity +25%; nutrient availability +20%
intervention: pH-targeted amendment: lime for acidic / gypsum + organic matter for sodic-alkaline
mechanism: pH gates bacterial:fungal ratio and P/micronutrient solubility; correcting unlocks existing nutrients before adding fertilizer.
source: FAO Soil pH Management; Weil & Brady Nature of Soils
title: Correct pH first, fertilize second

effect_size: Vegetation cover +40-70% in 2 yrs; SOC +0.3 tC/ha/yr
intervention: Rotational grazing + planned rest (holistic, 60-90 day recovery)
mechanism: Rest lets root reserves rebuild; trampling breaks capped soil improving infiltration; dung patch mosaic boosts plant heterogeneity.
source: FAO Grazing Management; Teague et al., 2016
title: Managed grazing reverses degradation

effect_size: Pollinator survival +40%; aquatic invertebrates +35%
intervention: IPM: pheromone traps + threshold spraying + 10m no-spray buffer near water
mechanism: Cuts non-target mortality; buffers stop drift into wetlands; natural enemies rebound within one season once broad-spectrum use stops.
source: IPBES Pollinators (2016); FAO IPM; Hallmann et al. flying insects 75% decline study
title: IPM + buffers stop silent pollinator collapse

domain: land use x climate x biodiversity
effect_size: Edge species +30%; carbon +50-100 tC/ha over 10 yrs
intervention: Riparian + degraded patch assisted natural regeneration (protect + mulch + exclude fire/grazing)
mechanism: ANR leverages soil seed bank and root suckers â€” 3-5x cheaper than planting; riparian shade cools water +2-3C saving fish/amphibians.
source: FAO Forest Restoration; IPCC AR6; Chazdon & Guariguata, 2016
title: Assisted natural regeneration beats planting on cost

effect_size: Evaporation -30-50%; soil temp -3-5C; SOC loss slowed 20%
intervention: Heavy organic mulch (5-10 t/ha straw/leaves) + shade trees on west edge
mechanism: Mulch decouples soil from hot air; cooler soil respires less CO2 and keeps microbes alive through heatwaves.
source: FAO Soil Mulching; IPCC AR6 Adaptation; Lal 2020
title: Mulch + shade as heat insurance

effect_size: Nematode diversity +30%; yield stability +15% in drought
intervention: 3-year rotation: cereal-legume-millet/oilseed + mycorrhizal inoculant on degraded patches
mechanism: Different root exudates select different microbes breaking pathogen build-up; mycorrhizae extend phosphorus scavenging 10x root radius.
source: FAO Crop Diversification; Bowles et al., Nature Food 2020
title: Rotation breaks monoculture disease-SOC trap

effect_size: N runoff -40-60%; wetland birds +25%
intervention: Constructed wetland / vegetated filter strip (2-5% lowland area)
mechanism: Sedges/reeds denitrify and trap sediment; doubles as breeding habitat â€” pollution control becomes habitat creation.
source: Ramsar; FAO Nutrient Management; Verhoeven et al.
title: Filter wetlands turn runoff into habitat

domain: land use x biodiversity x climate
effect_size: Interior forest species +35%; carbon +80 tC/ha
intervention: Wildlife corridor + canopy bridge (30-50m wide native planting linking fragments)
mechanism: Restores gene flow per metapopulation theory; wide corridors buffer edge heat/dryness preserving core microclimate.
source: IPBES 2019; CBD Corridors; Haddad et al., Science Advances 2015
title: Corridors reconnect fragmented humid forest

effect_size: Heat mortality -30%; water use -20%
intervention: Shift sowing 2-3 weeks earlier + heat-tolerant landraces + micro-irrigation at flowering
mechanism: Escapes terminal heat at anthesis (most sensitive stage); landrace diversity carries heat-shock genes lost in hybrids.
source: IPCC AR6 Adaptation; FAO Climate-Smart Seeds
title: Phenology shift dodges lethal heat

effect_size: SOC +0.15 tC/ha/yr vs burning; PM2.5 -80%; soil fauna +50%
intervention: Ban burning â†’ biochar from residues (2-5 t/ha) + compost
mechanism: Pyrolysis locks recalcitrant carbon for decades and raises CEC; compost seeds biology that biochar houses â€” synergy, not either/or.
source: IPCC AR6 (biochar CDR); FAO Biochar; Lehmann & Joseph 2015
title: Residues to biochar+compost, not smoke

contraindications: Do not apply gypsum on acidic soils; soil-test first
domain: soil x human impact x biodiversity
effect_size: pH -0.3-0.8 units in 2 seasons; infiltration x1.5-2; crop establishment +25-40%
intervention: Sodic soil reclamation: gypsum per soil test + dhaincha (Sesbania) green manure + good-quality water flushing
mechanism: Ca displaces Na on clay exchange, restoring aggregates; green manure adds organic acids + N, feeding microbes that stabilize new structure.
source: FAO Salt-Affected Soils Guide (2022); CSSRI Karnal reclamation trials
title: Gypsum + green manure reclaims sodic-alkaline soils

contraindications: Needs maintenance of emitters; filter water
effect_size: Water use -30-50%; yield same or +10-20%; runoff/pollution -40%
intervention: Deficit drip + soil-moisture scheduling (tensiometer/sensor at 15-30cm, irrigate at -30 to -50 kPa)
mechanism: Delivers water to root zone only, keeping inter-row dry refugia for ground fauna; mild deficit triggers deeper rooting + mycorrhizal colonization.
source: FAO Irrigation & Drainage No.66; IPCC AR6 Adaptation; Chartzoulakis & Bertaki review
title: Sensor-scheduled deficit drip saves water, spares fauna

contraindications: Avoid broad herbicide; cut-stump + uproot instead
effect_size: Native seedling recruitment x2-4 in 2 yrs; bird visits +30%; grazing value restored
intervention: Invasive shrub removal (Lantana camara / Prosopis juliflora): cut-stump + rootstock uproot + native reseeding
mechanism: Lantana allelopathy + dense shade suppresses natives; removal releases soil seed bank and light; natives re-establish mycorrhizal networks invasives disrupt.
source: IPBES Invasive Species Report (2023); CBD; Hiremath & Sundaram, Lantana studies
title: Remove Lantana/juliflora to unlock native seed banks

contraindications: Use local provenance seed; avoid exotic ornamentals
domain: land use x biodiversity x climate
effect_size: Native plant establishment +50-70%; pollinator constancy +35%; corridor use by birds +25%
intervention: Native seed orchard + hedgerow planting with local-provenance trees/shrubs (5+ species, fleshy-fruit + nectar mix)
mechanism: Local genotypes match phenology of local fauna; fleshy fruits feed frugivores that disperse seeds outward; mixed hedges flower sequentially closing hunger gaps.
source: CBD Ecosystem Restoration guidance; FAO Native Seeds; Rowland et al.
title: Local-provenance hedges + seed orchards that fauna actually use

contraindications: Keep 30% open water; avoid stocking exotic fish
domain: land use x biodiversity x climate
effect_size: Amphibian breeding +50-80%; dragonfly richness +40%; dry-season bird use +35%
intervention: Farm pond / wetland restoration: shallow gradients + native sedges + 30% open water + no exotic fish
mechanism: Gradients create tadpole/odonate microhabitats; sedges filter nutrients while sheltering nests; ponds act as drought refugia linking metapopulations.
source: Ramsar Convention guidance; FAO Wetlands; Rannap et al., pond restoration meta-analysis
title: Restore ponds/wetlands as drought refugia, not just storage

contraindications: Harvest + safely dispose hyperaccumulator biomass; do not graze
domain: human impact x soil x biodiversity
effect_size: Topsoil Pb/Cd -15-40% over 3-5 crops; soil fauna return +30%
intervention: Phytoremediation buffer: mustard/Brassica + vetiver + organic matter on contaminated margins
mechanism: Hyperaccumulators uptake metals; vetiver roots immobilize + stop leaching; organic matter binds residues while feeding remediating microbes.
source: FAO Polluted Soils remediation; Ali et al. review, Chemosphere; UNEP
title: Phytoremediation buffers for metal/pollutant margins

contraindications: Calibrate to soil test; do not cut P/K where deficient
domain: human impact x soil x biodiversity
effect_size: N use -20-30% same yield; N2O -25%; stream N -30-50%
intervention: Precision N: soil test + leaf-color chart + split dosing + urease inhibitor where advised
mechanism: Matching supply to crop demand curve cuts leaching/volatilization; soil fauna and aquatic invertebrates recover once N pulses stop.
source: FAO Fertilizer Code; IPCC AR6 WGIII; Zhang et al., N management meta-analysis
title: Soil-test precision N: same yield, far less leakage

contraindications: Never burn in bird breeding season or high wind
domain: human impact x climate x biodiversity
effect_size: Wildfire extent -40-60%; ground-nester survival +30%; SOC protected
intervention: Fire-smart mosaic: 5-10m mineral firebreaks + early cool-season controlled strips + grazing fuel-load control
mechanism: Patch mosaic breaks fire spread; cool burns consume litter without sterilizing soil seed bank; grazed fuel breaks double as habitat edges.
source: FAO Fire Management; UNCCD; Archibald et al., fire ecology
title: Mosaic firebreaks protect soil fauna and nests

contraindications: Avoid pesticide drift from neighbours; fence seedlings
effect_size: Garden pollinator richness +40-60%; household diet diversity +; spillover pollination to crops +15%
intervention: Homestead multi-layer garden: native fruit + vegetable + flower + compost pit + nest boxes
mechanism: Vertical structure mimics forest edge in tiny area; year-round flowers + nesting bridge seasonal gaps of monoculture fields.
source: FAO Urban-Rural linkages; IPBES Pollinators; Baldock et al., urban pollinator studies
title: Homestead gardens as pollinator reservoirs

contraindications: Orient N-S; prune to avoid excess crop shading
domain: climate x land use x biodiversity
effect_size: Wind erosion -50%; crop water demand -10-20%; bird perching/nesting +30%
intervention: Shelterbelts: 2-3 row native windbreak (tall + medium + shrub) on windward/west edge
mechanism: Cuts desiccating wind + dust abrasion; evening shade lowers canopy temperature; linear trees double as movement corridor.
source: FAO Agroforestry; IPCC AR6 Adaptation; Brandle et al., shelterbelt review
title: Shelterbelts cut wind, water loss, and isolation

contraindications: eDNA complements, not replaces, field surveys
effect_size: Detection of cryptic species +30-50%; survey cost -40% per site after setup
intervention: Bioindicator monitoring: eDNA water sampling + pitfall/bee-bowl transects twice a season
mechanism: eDNA detects amphibians/fish missed visually; standardized insect transects give comparable richness trends that justify which intervention worked.
source: CBD Monitoring guidance; IPBES; Thomsen & Willerslev eDNA review
title: Measure biodiversity right: eDNA + standard transects

effect_size: Management signal detectable in 12-24 months; avoids mistaking noise for gain
intervention: Soil health card protocol: 0-15cm SOC (Walkley-Black/lab) + pH strip + infiltration ring, same points yearly
mechanism: Fixed-point repeat measurement separates real SOC gain from spatial noise; infiltration reveals biology faster than lab carbon.
source: FAO Soil Health / Soil Doctors; Weil & Brady
title: Soil health cards: prove your carbon gain

contraindications: Do not drain natural wetlands; only farm waterlogging
effect_size: Waterlogging days -50%; root disease -30%; dry-season soil fauna +25%
intervention: Raised beds + field surface drainage + waterlogging-tolerant legume (sesbania) in low patches
mechanism: Beds keep root crowns aerated; drains stop anoxia that kills mycorrhizae; tolerant legumes keep N flowing where main crop drowns.
source: FAO Drainage & Waterlogging; IPCC AR6 Adaptation
title: Raised beds + drains beat waterlogging without losing wetlands

contraindications: Do not till nesting banks in breeding season
effect_size: Ground-nesting bee occupancy +50-70%; cavity-nester use +40%; pollination +20%
intervention: Nesting habitat: 1-2 sqm undisturbed bare bank + pithy-stem bundles + no-till corner
mechanism: 70% of wild bees nest in ground, not hives; undisturbed banks + stems close the nesting (not flower) bottleneck that flower strips alone miss.
source: IPBES Pollinators (2016); FAO Pollinator-friendly farming; Antoine & Forrest
title: Nest sites, not just flowers: the non-obvious pollinator fix

contraindications: Follow vet withdrawal periods; never overdose
domain: soil x biodiversity x human impact
effect_size: Dung removal rate x1.5-2; pasture fouling -30%; soil beetle richness +40%
intervention: Dung-fauna smart worming: faecal-egg-count targeted treatment + avoid whole-herd ivermectin in beetle season
mechanism: Blanket ivermectin residues kill dung beetles that bury dung (= SOC + parasite control); targeted dosing keeps beetles alive to do the work free.
source: FAO Livestock & Environment; Lumaret & Errouissi; VerdÃº et al.
title: Save dung beetles: targeted worming builds soil free

contraindications: Needs agreed bylaws; elite capture risk
domain: human impact x land use x biodiversity
effect_size: Vegetation cover +40-60% in 2-3 yrs; rule compliance +50% vs open access
intervention: Community exclosure + bylaws: rest 1-2 seasons, cut-and-carry, guarded native planting
mechanism: Ostrom-style clear boundaries + graduated sanctions solve free-riding; rest lets root reserves + seed set recover before reuse.
source: FAO Commons; Ostrom Governing the Commons; CBD
title: Community exclosures with bylaws beat open grazing

contraindications: Match shade % to crop light needs (30-40% max for cereals)
domain: climate x land use x biodiversity
effect_size: Canopy temp -2-4C; bird/insect richness +35-50%; income diversity +30%
intervention: Multi-strata intercrop: timber/fruit overstory (30% shade) + crop + understory legume/vegetable
mechanism: Stratified canopy partitions light/water/niches; birds + parasitoids persist in canopy even when ground crop is harvested.
source: FAO Agroforestry; IPCC AR6; Perfecto & Vandermeer coffee multistrata studies
title: Multi-strata cropping: farm in 3D for heat + habitat
